full_judgment:
That respondent No. 3, Basic Bank Limited as a plaintiff filed an Artha Rin Suit No. 195 of 2017 against the defendant-petitioner for realization the loan amount of Taka 10,38,69,999.44 (Taka Ten crore, Thirty-eight lac, Sixty-nine thousand, Nine hundred ninety-nine and Forty-four paisa) which was subsequently decreed ex-parte vide its order dated 10-10-2018. The decree was signed on 14-10-2018. Subsequently, the decree-holder bank put the said decree into execution by way of filing an Artha Jari Case No. 2 of 2019. During pending the Artha Jari Case the defendant-petitioner filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure along with section 57 and 6(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 before the execution Court below for selling out his mortgaged property in his own initiatives to adjust the loan money of the respondent bank which was rejected by the impugned order. Being aggrieved, the petitioner has preferred this application before this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the instant Rule and stay. 

 5. The petitioner has stated in his application that he did not know anything about the instant Artha Rin Suit. The suit was decreed ex-parte. The petitioner came to know about this case for the first time on 19-5-2019. The petitioner is now willing to adjust the decretal amount through selling out his mortgaged property at his own initiative otherwise the petitioner will suffer irreparable loss and injury but the execution Court below failed to appreciate his application and thereby passed the impugned order which is illegal and not sustainable in law. 

 "(1) Where an order for the sale of immovable property has been made, if the judgment-debtor can satisfy the Court that there is reason to believe that the amount of the decree may be raised by the mortgage or lease or private sale of such property, or some part thereof, or of any other immovable property of the judgment-debtor, the Court may, on his application, postpone the sale of the property comprised in the order for sale on such terms and for such period as it thinks proper, to enable him to raise the amount. 

 Provided that all monies payable under such mortgage, lease or sale shall be paid, not to the judgment-debtor, but save in so far as a decree-holder is entitled to set-off such money under the provisions of rule 72, into Court: Provided also that no mortgage, lease, or sale under this Rule shall become absolute until it has been confirmed by the Court. 

 (3) Nothing in this rule shall be deemed to apply to a sale of property directed to be sold in execution of a decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of or charge on, such property." 

 11. However, it is clear from sub-rule (3) that this Rule does not apply to a sale in the enforcement of a mortgage. In case of execution of a decree in a mortgage suit there is no scope for private sale it must be sold by public auction. There is no conflict between rule 83 of the Code and the provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and as such there is no bar to apply rule 83 of the Code in execution proceeding initiated to levy  execution of a decree of the Artha Rin Adalat but when it comes to the sale of the mortgaged property sub-rule (3) of rule 83 of the Code comes into play and the Adalat cannot permit the  private sale of the mortgaged property.
